label: early-prefix combination detector (t=2-4, prev token s/t/d)
explanation: Sparse feature (0.06% of steps). About 72% of activation mass falls in the original phase at t=2-4 (peak t=3), and it looks like a lookup on the specific first 3-4 tokens: previous token s (18.8x lift, about half the mass), also t or d; the token two back is u/s/v/1/y/d; the first token is h/1/b/v/j/e/y/u. The strongest cases are prefixes like h u s, h v v s, h u d s. Magnitude is highest when the first token is h and the previous token is s. A smaller copy-phase component (about 26% of mass, rising at late recall_idx, out_tok h or b) is not captured. It does not fire at t=0-1, is rare after t=5 in the original phase, and almost never fires on the delimiter. The best compact conjunction only reaches F1 about 0.22 (dev mass recall 0.44). Prev_tok=s alone has precision 0.02, so the feature responds to a combination of prefix tokens rather than any single variable.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=3 (+5.20), t=3 & prev_tok=t (+4.66), t=3 & prev_tok=d (+4.46), prev_tok=s (+3.91), phase=2 & out_tok=h (+3.58), phase=2 & in_tok=j (+3.51). Lower it: recall_idx=1 (-3.13), in_tok=y (-3.06), in_tok=t (-3.00), orig_idx=-1 (-2.78).
